name: TinyZKP Agent Proof Policy
summary: Recommended policy for AI agents, agent supervisors, and backend automations that decide when to mint, attach, verify, and escalate TinyZKP proof receipts.

positioning.primary_use: Proof receipts for high-value agent actions and state transitions
best_for: Agents that mutate money, records, permissions, inventory, compliance state, or customer-visible status
Agent supervisors that need independent verification of workflow checkpoints
Backend tool calls where a downstream service should verify a state transition without replay
Audit and reconciliation agents that publish periodic receipt-bearing checkpoints
not_for: UI-only interactions with no durable state change
Claims that cannot be encoded into the live proof template or a reviewed custom statement
Private-input claims without a documented template, explicit review status, and supported verifier path

mint_receipt_when: An agent action changes durable external state.
A tool-call batch affects money, balances, quotas, inventory, records, permissions, or compliance state.
A customer, auditor, downstream service, or supervisor agent will rely on the output.
A checkpoint replaces replay, manual audit export, support evidence, or self-hosted prover operations.
skip_receipt_when: The output has no durable state transition.
No recipient will inspect or store the receipt.
The statement would require private inputs or custom semantics that have not been reviewed.
always_attach: what the receipt does not prove
never_send_as_transparent_parameters: personal data not required for the public statement

reject_or_review_when: The proof format is below the current accepted floor.
The receipt claims a template, privacy mode, or verifier path not documented in public metadata.
The statement does not match the workflow output the agent is presenting.

escalation_triggers: The proof statement is not an additive state transition covered by accumulator_step.
The workflow needs private-input handling, masking, or secrets.
The verifier must run on-chain, air-gapped, or inside a restricted runtime.
The workflow needs reserved concurrency, custom spend controls, or contractual support targets.
The receipt is customer-, auditor-, counterparty-, or regulator-visible and requires procurement review.
The trace size or latency profile suggests Compute planning.
